name: str_wrap
title: Wrap words into nicely formatted paragraphs

origin.description: Wrap each string into a paragraph and join the lines with newlines.
origin.usage: str_wrap(string, width = 80, indent = 0, exdent = 0, whitespace_only = TRUE)

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Target line width. A width of 0 or less is treated as 1, so each word is on its own line.

arguments.name: indent
arguments.text: Extra spaces before the first line. A whole number, zero or more.

arguments.name: exdent
arguments.text: Extra spaces before every line after the first. A whole number, zero or more.

arguments.name: whitespace_only
arguments.text: If true, break only at whitespace. If false, a non-word character such as / can also break.

origin.details: The line breaks are stringi's Knuth-Plass wrap. Each paragraph's lines are joined with a newline. A missing string stays missing.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as string.
origin.example:
thanks_path <- file.path(R.home("doc"), "THANKS")
thanks <- str_c(readLines(thanks_path), collapse = "\n")
thanks <- word(thanks, 1, 3, fixed("\n\n"))
cat(str_wrap(thanks), "\n")
cat(str_wrap(thanks, width = 40), "\n")
cat(str_wrap(thanks, width = 60, indent = 2), "\n")
cat(str_wrap(thanks, width = 60, exdent = 2), "\n")
cat(str_wrap(thanks, width = 0, exdent = 2), "\n")

translation.description: Wrap each string into a paragraph and join the lines with newlines. The result is a list. A missing string is stringi._na.NA.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Target line width. A width of 0 or less is treated as 1, so each word is on its own line.

arguments.name: indent
arguments.text: Extra spaces before the first line. A whole number, zero or more.

translation.details: The line breaks are stringi's Knuth-Plass wrap. Each paragraph's lines are joined with a newline. A missing string stays missing. The Python result is a list, and a missing string is stringi._na.NA.
translation.value: A character vector the same length as string.
translation.example:
from pathlib import Path
from stringr.pattern import fixed
from stringr.word import word
from stringr.wrap import str_wrap
thanks = "\n".join(Path("/usr/share/R/doc/THANKS").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines())
thanks = word(thanks, 1, 3, sep=fixed("\n\n"))[0]
print(str_wrap(thanks)[0])
print(str_wrap(thanks, width=40)[0])
print(str_wrap(thanks, width=60, indent=2)[0])
print(str_wrap(thanks, width=60, exdent=2)[0])
print(str_wrap(thanks, width=0, exdent=2)[0])
